headline: Specialized nucleic acid language models target regulatory design and RNA prediction
label: Specialized Nucleic Acid Foundation Models
summary: Between 18 and 23 November 2026, models add task-specific pretraining and explicit control to nucleotide sequence design and prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is adapting nucleotide foundation models to specific sequence tasks and explicit design objectives. BQDNA and HGDNA contribute tokenization and architecture advances for autoregressive genomic language models, with BQDNA using a context-aware scalar quantization tokenizer and HGDNA using overlapping k-mer tokenization. A second group steers generation toward defined targets: GENECraft couples a genomic language model with a functional oracle without training, REGAL uses reinforcement learning to program enhancer regulatory grammar, ARCADE controls codon metrics via activation engineering, and GenNA conditions generation on natural-language annotations. LncRFM targets lncRNA prediction with its own corpus and benchmark. The CRISPR spacer study differs in framing, treating refinement as constrained search with a thermodynamic objective. The items vary in task and architecture but share a shift toward explicit control of model outputs.
